t1.text: Clinic floor · triage and clinic line

s1.text:
Try this (press Play)

1. Clinic line (doctor): Godfrey is with you, the timer runs. Finish visit (F): choose Pharmacy, then home, a follow-up in a month, a day. The follow-up ticket fills in on the side.
2. Press N, or Call next: Mercy (L2 · Orange) is called. Text sent, code on the waiting-room screen. He's here, or Call again, or Didn't come.
3. Screen: what the waiting room sees (codes and rooms only).
4. Triage (1, or switch user to the nurse): Start triage, tick None of these, type the observations, consciousness and mobility. Tether's triage engine gives the level (L1 to L4) with its reasons and NEWS2/TEWS; changing it asks why. L1 opens resus. Send to a line.
5. Floor (3): everyone on the floor by stage.
6. Running late, End session (move, hand over, didn't wait).
7. New: In room / Short break / Called away pauses calls and tells the desk and screen. Triage › Re-checks: Joseph is due (hourly obs); re-check him and watch him move up. Wait ~15 s: Fatuma's lab result returns her to the line. Calling Joseph or Hassan shows their needs. Switch to Diabetes Clinic to see trends.

Tweaks: role Doctor / Nurse, First run, Offline, Dark.

s2.text:
Assumed (your decisions pending)

• Per-sign amber/red tags on observations are draft display limits; the level always comes from the engine
• Triage uses Tether's existing triage engine v2 (NEWS2 + SATS/TEWS, Step 0 life threats, overridable with a reason). The prototype mimics it; the build calls the engine
• Line order: L2, L3, back from tests, then L4 by arrival; never shown to patients
• Waiting-room screen shows booking codes only
• Didn't come: first time moves to the end, second time ends the visit
• Follow-up booking from the doctor uses the same booking engine and ticket
• The visit record (clerking, prescribing, orders) stays in the clinician workspace

s3.text:
Look: MedSync Tide, same as the reception desk

Same sidebar (today card, rail), same table and side-panel patterns, same ticket. New here: amber for vital signs needing attention, which is a clinical signal, so allowed. Red only for danger signs and emergency.
